request.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Original production game sprite sheet for a tower management simulation. Contemporary premium PIXEL ART: intentional visible square pixel clusters, hard stepped edges, clean dark navy pixel outlines, controlled warm amber/cream/coral interiors and cool teal/blue structure palette, expressive compact figures, simplified readable silhouettes. No painterly texture, no blur, no antialiasing, no smooth vector curves. Fixed straight-on orthographic side cutaway camera, no isometric perspective. No text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, watermark, panel borders or gutters. Canvas EXACTLY 1536x1024 pixels. EXACT regular grid 2 columns by 8 rows, row-major order; cell dimensions 768x128. Grid begins at x=0,y=0 and ends at x=1536,y=1024. No margins, no gutters. Invisible cell boundaries at exact integer multiples of cell width/height. All sixteen room cells fill their own 768x128 rectangle edge to edge, thin horizontal floor and ceiling within each cell, furniture and walls fully contained in their own cell. Exactly two rooms per row, exactly eight equal-height rows. No exterior building, no tower composition. Row 1: office with desks and monitors; condo with sofa, kitchenette and plant. Row 2: hotel bedroom with bed and luggage; shop with shelves and checkout. Row 3: fast-food counter with trays; restaurant with dining tables and kitchen. Row 4: medical clinic with exam bed and cabinet; security room with cameras and console. Row 5: housekeeping with carts and linen; party hall with tables and balloons. Row 6: cinema with screen and seating; metro platform. Row 7: reception lobby; parking garage with parked cars. Row 8: recycling room with sorting bins; elevator machinery room with motors. Rooms are wide and shallow, furniture deliberately compact to fit 128 pixel height.

production_limitations: Generated pixel art retains some soft tonal shading inside pixel clusters; it is not a hand-indexed fixed palette atlas.

People remain wholly within 256x256 cells, with slight scale/baseline drift and similar repeated poses; six frames per character are not hand-authored locomotion. Fourth row is one formal VIP/wedding character, not separate emergency and bride archetypes.
Incidental parking P glyphs exist in transport/UI despite the no-text prompt; icon semantics otherwise match.
White cutout sheets are RGB, not native transparent PNG. White interiors need preservation by the packer; global white-to-alpha removes light costume/cloud details.
Exterior background normalization may erase connected pale details; the cloud is primarily a white silhouette with navy outline. Cathedral ceremony is a full-scene cell, not a character cutout.
Rooms contain some baked-in figures and nonuniform furniture scale; original row heights were normalized to exact 128px by nearest neighbor. Room wall/floor strokes are artwork, not atlas gutters.
Engine-size packing, animation playback, silhouette legibility at actual game resolution and integrated gameplay remain unverified by this source-only worker.
